official.deadline_note: doc.funds runs on an annual call; on 2026-10-10 the official page stated 'Currently no submissions', with the current round's decisions scheduled for late November 2026 by the FWF Scientific Board.
official.application_cycle: Annual call; current round decided late November 2026 (doc.funds jury meeting 12-13 November 2026); about 5 projects funded per call, volume about EUR 2.5 million
official.status_note: The official page states 'Currently no submissions'; the next decisions for the current round are scheduled for late November 2026 based on the recommendation of the international doc.funds jury.
benefits: Personnel costs for 5 to 10 doctoral candidates (2026 standard rate: EUR 2,832.10 per month per doctoral candidate at 30 h/week; EUR 50,220 per year, gross including the employer's contribution)
Training costs of up to EUR 5,000 per doctoral candidate position per year
Funding for a maximum period of 48 months
Call volume of about EUR 2.5 million, with about 5 projects funded per call
eligibility: All Austrian research institutions entitled to grant doctoral degrees, where at least 5 researchers or arts-based researchers join to form a consortium to implement a project
The existing doctoral programme must have been running for at least 2 years on the date of the application deadline

Binding basic funding by the lead research institution (and any partner research institutions), i.e. provision of all necessary infrastructure, financial means for ongoing operation, and ensuring institutional affiliation
Involvement of doctoral students in a focused and consistent research framework; education through research
Existing structures and procedures for admission and selection of doctoral candidates, supervision and monitoring, suitable working conditions, and completion of the doctoral programme
Based on and oriented towards international standards
Consortium of at least 5 researchers from universities and universities of applied sciences with outstanding research records by FWF standards
Balanced gender distribution in the consortium; at least one third of the consortium should be made up of the underrepresented gender
requirements: At least 5 researchers must join the consortium; the consortium composition is one of the deciding factors in review
No applications are accepted for additional funding for ongoing FWF-funded projects from the Doctoral Programs, doc.funds or doc.funds.connect programmes
Application submitted online via the elane portal during the annual window
See the application guidelines and the doc.funds checklist for further details
documents: Template publication record of principal investigator
Scientific disciplines / Code Statistics Austria classification document
Information on accounting for career breaks, checklist career breaks and form for career interruptions, if applicable
Information on Funding for Equality Measures
selection_criteria: Approval in late November 2026 by the FWF Scientific Board based on the recommendation of the international doc.funds jury
Recommendations are prepared at the doc.funds jury meeting on 12-13 November 2026 on the basis of international peer review and hearings
The consortium's composition, including gender balance (at least one third from the underrepresented gender), is one of the deciding factors in the review and evaluation process
About 5 projects are funded per call
coverage: Personnel costs for 5 to 10 doctoral candidates (2026 rate: EUR 2,832.10 per month per doctoral candidate at 30 h/week)
Training costs of up to EUR 5,000 per doctoral candidate position per year
Programme duration of a maximum of 48 months
application_method: Apply online via the elane portal when the annual call window opens
The application must come from a consortium of at least 5 researchers at eligible Austrian research institutions, entitled to grant doctoral degrees
Binding basic funding from the lead research institution (and partners) must be secured as part of the application
official.application_route: This is an institutional programme: universities or consortia of at least 5 researchers apply via elane for an existing doctoral programme; individual doctoral candidates are then recruited by those institutions.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality rule is published; the target group is Austrian research institutions entitled to grant doctoral degrees.
official.international_eligibility: The grant funds Austrian institutions; doctoral candidates within the funded programme are recruited through the institutions' own admission and selection procedures, which are oriented towards international standards.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to scientific or arts-based research training across all disciplines at institutions entitled to grant doctoral degrees.
official.research_requirement: The programme must place doctoral students in a focused and consistent research framework (education through research) and must have existing structures and procedures for admission and selection of doctoral candidates, supervision and monitoring, suitable working conditions, and completion of the doctoral programme.
official.description: The FWF presents doc.funds as funding that strengthens doctoral training programmes in Austria: it facilitates scientific or arts-based education and training for doctoral students in existing structured doctoral programmes and helps universities sustainably reinforce their education and training structures in the long term.
official.program_type: Structured doctoral programme funding (doc.funds) for doctoral training programmes at Austrian research institutions

verification.notes: The FWF funding-portfolio URL for the former 'Doctoral Programmes' now resolves to doc.funds, the renamed programme; its page and the FWF 2026 personnel costs page were read in full on 2026-10-10. Funding headcount (5 to 10 doctoral candidates), training costs of up to EUR 5,000 per candidate position per year, the 48-month maximum, the jury timetable and the 'currently no submissions' state are published verbatim. Note that older records quoting EUR 1,960 per month are outdated: the 2026 doctoral candidate rate is EUR 2,832.10 per month.

applicant_utility.summary: Do not apply to doc.funds as an individual - the FWF funds the doctoral programme, not the student: a consortium of at least 5 Austrian researchers with an existing doctoral programme (at least 2 years old) and binding basic funding from the lead institution submits the application. Your route in is the university: look for Austrian universities running FWF-funded doc.funds programmes and apply for a funded doctoral position within one, where the FWF pays your personnel costs at the 2026 doctoral candidate rate of EUR 2,832.10 per month at 30 h/week plus up to EUR 5,000 per year of training costs. Decisions for the current round come in late November 2026, so vacancies within newly funded programmes typically open for the following intake.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Prospective doctoral researchers targeting Austrian universities, and Austrian consortia of at least five researchers who run a doctoral programme that has existed for at least two years and can show institutional basic funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify Austrian universities with active FWF doc.funds or doc.funds.connect programmes in your field before considering an independent PhD application
For institutional applicants: confirm the doctoral programme has run continuously for at least 2 years by the application deadline
For institutional applicants: secure written binding basic funding from the lead institution (and partners) covering infrastructure and ongoing operation
Prepare the template publication record and the Statistics Austria scientific disciplines code for the consortium
Check that no consortium member's ongoing FWF Doctoral Programme, doc.funds or doc.funds.connect project would make this a top-up application
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a single strong professor can apply - fewer than 5 consortium researchers fails the programme's core rule
Applying while another FWF doctoral-programme funding for an ongoing project is active, which is excluded
Weak evidence of institutional commitment (no binding basic funding, no infrastructure), which undermines the review
As a doctoral candidate, emailing the FWF directly instead of applying to the hiring university's programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Only personnel costs (5 to 10 doctoral candidates) and up to EUR 5,000 per position per year of training costs are funded; institutional overhead, research equipment and living costs beyond the doctoral salary are covered by the institution or the candidate.
document_audit: The consortium composition and its gender balance (at least one third from the underrepresented gender) are reviewed, so the consortium list matters, not just the science
The programme must evidence existing admission, supervision and completion procedures - younger programmes struggle here
Career-break documentation uses the standard FWF forms; consortia should fill them in rather than argue the case narratively
doc.funds and doc.funds.connect are separate programmes and their Phases through PROFI need care when an institution runs both
alerts: The programme is financed with funds from the Fonds Zukunft Oesterreich, and volume is about EUR 2.5 million for roughly 5 projects per call
The doc.funds jury meets in mid-November with decisions in late November, so institutional timelines should work backwards from that
This record replaces the old 'FWF Doctoral Programs' branding: search under doc.funds on the FWF site, as the former programme URL no longer resolves
Doctoral candidates employed in doc.funds positions are paid by FWF personnel-cost rates, which are adjusted annually
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Institutions assemble a consortium of at least 5 researchers with a mature doctoral programme, apply via elane in the annual window, pass the international jury hearing, and the Scientific Board decides in late November.
